questions.question: At night, what is the minimum following distance a motorcyclist should keep?
questions.explanation: It is harder to see and judge distances at night than during the day. Keep at least three seconds of distance behind the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to notice if the vehicle stops and to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve your view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve your view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign where indicated. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to see if anything is coming. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Keep your intentions unknown from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals and brake light. Position yourself properly in the lane. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to maintain balance.
Maintain your speed to improve traction.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery roads when possible. If you cannot avoid them, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as you can.

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind while riding?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what lane position should you use?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are similar.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes several times.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back of the group.

questions.question: The body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks will likely be in their system three hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. If someone drinks seven drinks in three hours and three more hours pass, about four drinks will remain in their system.

questions.question: When a motorcycle crash happens, most riders are traveling:

options.text: On a trip of more than 30 miles.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen when riders are going slower than 30 mph. These crashes usually occur on short trips of less than five miles.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to help you balance.

questions.question: To stop quickly on wet pavement, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you need to stop quickly on a slippery surface. Apply the front brake gradually to avoid locking it.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and go straight. Gradually brake only on the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance at night to stay safe. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see better. Use your high beam, unless you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate to escape a wobble—it will make things worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: A helmet will not protect you well if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT and state standards and fit snugly all around. It should have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Which of the following is not important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all around your head, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: The front brake provides what percent of a motorcycle's braking power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous by encouraging them to follow you faster.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black lettering show road rules like speed limits. Drivers must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to be split up.
Riders get to their destination more quickly in a close group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders get to their destination more quickly in a close group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group is better than spreading out because the group uses less road space, is easier to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights and during passes.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased by a dog, downshift and approach it slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.
